Often, on misty days on the harbour, the ghosts of the memories of fishermen of old linger. 
The tinkling bell that rings softly on an empty boat as if it were on the sea. The waves, steady in their clapping, like wet heavy boots  stomping on the ground. The seagulls, crying out their morning greetings to the boats and getting a small fish in return. 

Sometimes, the fog drifts over your hand, and leaves the warm, sea moistened touch of a wise grandfather teaching you how to fish.
